subject: Pilot tier selection, rollback gates, and sandbox fit for NeuraHealth
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@neurahealth.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@neurahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot tier selection and upgrade/downgrade questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at NeuraHealth liked the latency and the KV caching examples. We're starting to sketch the pilot scope and have a few practical packaging questions before we lock timelines:

- If we start on the Compact tier for a pilot and need to scale mid-pilot, how does upgrade proration work? Do seats/burst capacity and feature entitlements activate immediately?
- Conversely, if we find features we don't need and want to step down, is there an automated downgrade path or is that a manual change with prorated credits?
- Can you outline what features are considered "core" vs "addon" (specifically streaming, function/tool calling, and per-route analytics)? We want to avoid unexpected charges.

Procurement (cc'd Tom) also asked whether you offer any trial credits or a reduced-price evaluation window tied to measured SLOs. Budget is constrained and they want a clear cost containment plan if we scale.

Can we get a short written playbook we can share with our platform team — preferably a single-page matrix that maps tier | feature | upgrade/downgrade behavior? If possible, include accepted rollback triggers (latency, error rate, token cost delta).

Appreciate it — Olivia

Olivia Park
Head of Platform, NeuraHealth
olivia.park@neurahealth.com
From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@neurahealth.com>
Cc: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@neurahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot tier selection and upgrade/downgrade questions

Hi Olivia / Tom,

Great questions — thanks for laying them out. I put together the short matrix and a pricing proposal and attached both (tier_matrix_v3.csv, pricing_proposal_v3.pdf). High-level answers here so you can share quickly with engineering and procurement:

1) Upgrades mid-pilot:
- Upgrade is immediate for entitlements (capacity, feature toggles). Performance/throughput becomes available within the next allocation window (typically 5-15 minutes for hosted allocations).
- Billing is prorated: you pay the difference between tiers for the remainder of the billing period. For pilots we can offer pro-rata credits applied at next invoice if requested (see discounts below).

2) Downgrades and credits:
- Downgrades are manual via Console or API; entitlements are removed at the start of the next billing period to avoid mid-period disruption.
- If you must step down immediately, we can offer a credit model versus a hard refund — we note the token/throughput delta and apply a prorated credit. We recommend a short communication window (24 hours) to schedule the change to avoid KV cache churn.

3) Core vs Addon (short list):
- Core: text generation, embeddings, streaming response.
- Addon (metered/feature flags): function/tool calling (per-call metering), per-route advanced analytics (retention beyond default), dedicated burst pools.

4) Rollback gates we suggest including in your playbook (baseline numbers are placeholders — we can make these concrete after a short traffic profile):
- Latency increase > 25% sustained over 5 minutes
- Error rate > 2% for any 5-minute window
- Per-token cost delta > 30% relative to baseline for high-volume routes

5) Trial credits and discounts:
- For pilot deals we commonly provide a timeboxed trial credit and a 10% pilot discount on committed capacity if you sign within the trial window. Ben (cc) will propose a commercial construct.

Next steps:
- I've attached matrix and proposal for your review.
- If useful, we can run a 30-minute runbook walk-through with your platform team next week. Proposed times: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

Happy to hop on a call.

Best,
Mina
Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: tier_matrix_v3.csv (CSV), pricing_proposal_v3.pdf (PDF)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@neurahealth.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@neurahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot tier selection and upgrade/downgrade questions

Olivia / Mina,

Quick commercial note from my side — thanks for surfacing the downgrade risk. For NH we can do the following to reduce procurement risk:

- Pilot credit: $50k of consumption credit applied during the 90-day pilot.
- If an upgrade is required mid-pilot, pro-rata billing applies; if NeuraHealth steps down for technical reasons and we agree it’s due to platform regressions, we will apply a discretionary credit equal to the incremental spend attributable to the upgrade (requires a short post-mortem).
- I'll attach a short rollback playbook that maps metrics -> action (NeuraHealth_Rollback_Playbook.xlsx).

Deal optics: if you commit to a 12-month Dedicated reservation after pilot, we can offer a one-time 15% commitment discount on top of the standard tiers (details in the attached proposal).

Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: NeuraHealth_Rollback_Playbook.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@neurahealth.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@neurahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot tier selection and upgrade/downgrade questions

Thanks Mina and Ben — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from Procurement and Platform:

- Procurement: Tom needs the credit and discount mechanics written into the SOW. Can you provide a language draft (simple clause) that we can hand to legal? Also confirm whether discounts are net of marketplace fees (we plan to run this via our GCP marketplace subscription).
- Platform: we prefer non-disruptive downgrades (i.e., windows where traffic is drained before entitlement removal). Can you formalize the 24-hour schedule you referenced?

We have a hard cap for pilot spend at $60k (without prior approval). The $50k pilot credit sounds right provided the remaining delta is explainable.

Can we lock a short runbook session for Wed 07/07 10:00 PT? If you can send a calendar invite and a one-page SOW clause, we’ll circulate to legal and platform.

Olivia
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@neurahealth.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot tier selection and upgrade/downgrade questions

Thanks everyone — adding a quick governance note from Redwood leadership so procurement/legal have a clear signal.

- Approved commercial fallback: We can confirm a $50k pilot credit and a fixed pilot discount of 10% for the 90-day evaluation. If NeuraHealth converts to a 12-month Dedicated reservation within 30 days of pilot end, Redwood will apply an additional 15% commitment discount (stacking rules and marketplace fees to be clarified in SOW language).
- Operational rollback cadence: We will formalize a 24-hour drain window for downgrades with an explicit revert path if metrics exceed rollback gates. The default gates are Mina's suggested thresholds; engineering can tune them during the runbook.
- Legal clause: Ben, please send the one-paragraph SOW wording (we should keep it non-binding for pilot credit application but explicit on conversion terms).

Ben / Mina — please share the calendar invite and the SOW snippet. Olivia / Tom — looking forward to the runbook session on 07/07.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
